steps: Camera as given: composed spot (2.030, 28.300, 1.720), turned -180.00 degrees; the plate's spot (the slide's start) (2.030, 29.500, 1.720).

checks.about: The eye stands 1.70 m above the view's floor (height 0.02 m) (allowed 1.5 to 1.9 m for still_life).
The camera is level (tilt -0.00 degrees): the planner never tilts; an overview raises the eye.
The street's lines meet behind the camera: it faces down the street.
checks.fix: Turn the camera to face up the street.

checks.about: The lowest story thing is no-2-man-1, reaching 0.715 down (limit 0.7).
Story things in the button strip (0.45 to 0.95 down) end at: no-2 gate 0.51, no-2-man-1 0.50, no-2-man-2 0.32, no-2-man-3 0.16, no-2-man-5 0.54, no-2-man-6 0.42, no-2-man-7 0.26 across (limit 0.95).

The story things stand together in the street: the loneliest, man-4, is 0.19 m from man-5 (limit 0.3 m between footprints).

The spots that can be worked out before rendering (middle of no-2 gate 0.51, 0.53; middle of the story things 0.29, 0.60) span 0.22 x 0.07 (the plan keeps them inside 0.3 x 0.4 so the brightest parts and the warm light have room within the rule's 0.4 x 0.5).

In the bottom-left quarter, where the eye enters, the boxes cover: no-2-man-1 3.4% (over its 2%), no-2-man-2 3.6% (over its 2%), no-2-man-3 3.2% (over its 2%), no-2-man-5 1.9%, no-2-man-6 2.8% (over its 2%), no-2-man-7 2.9% (over its 2%), no-2-drum-diesel 1.4% (over its 1%) (limit 1% a thing, 2% for a story thing in a crowd shot; a box covers more than the thing in it, so these are upper bounds).
checks.fix: Confirm on the render (the shot checker measures the real outlines); if it holds, move no-2-man-1, no-2-man-2, no-2-man-3, no-2-man-6, no-2-man-7, no-2-drum-diesel out of the bottom-left quarter.

checks.fix: Move no-2-man-7 sideways into a gap, or check on the render.

checks.about: The 1.20 m slide brings the nearest painted thing, wages envelope (its nearest corner 5.13 m away at the end), 1.234 times nearer; the painting's 2672 rows allow 1.286; the longest slide for it is 1.47 m.
The painted ground at the frame's bottom edge (2.92 m away) comes 1.411 times nearer (not counted: nobody has judged whether its softness shows; --count-ground counts it).

Casting the film frame's corners and edge middles onto the floor every 10% of the slide, the plate needs a lens of at least 63.53 degrees (with the 0.03 fade band at its edge); the house plate lens is 64.4 (film 60.4 + 4.0); the camera may turn 1.38 degrees each way inside it.
For the slide's worst magnification the plate would need 2564 rows of real detail; the painter returns 2672 (the house plate is 1536 x 2730).
